decisions.reason: As a newly launched, close-to-core classic door lever handle in a growing market, it is likely to be retained because there is no clear sign of performance below aspiration and the large firm's portfolio slack can absorb short-run uncertainty.

A door lever handle family fits the firm's established system-oriented offer and broad-range strategy, so absent negative results management would likely keep it rather than reallocate resources immediately.

This door handle design is near the existing business and likely benefits from the firm's design capabilities, though as a design variant it faces a somewhat higher chance of later portfolio pruning if demand disappoints.

Because it is another close-to-core door handle design launched only recently, boundedly rational management would usually allow more time for market feedback unless it clearly falls short of aspirations.
A lever handle family supports the firm's breadth across building projects and budgets, making retention likely while the firm assesses its fit and sales within the existing assortment.

The electronic access system strongly matches the firm's move toward digital building organization and was presented as technologically distinctive, so management is especially likely to continue backing it.
